{"content":"An unchanged calendar in a queued draft can reverse another editor's move. After Save moves an event from A to B, the queue reloads it from B. A second editor's title-only draft still contains calendarId A. This code selects A and moves the event back.","codeSuggestion":"","assessment":"P2. Save treats an unchanged calendar as an explicit move request.","rationale":"applyCalendarEventDraft compares title and date values with the baseline. Calendar selection has no equivalent comparison before assignment at line 121. test_overlappingEditsAfterCalendarMove changes the calendar in both drafts. The queued-occurrence test also changes every draft's calendar, so both tests omit this case.","recommendation":"change","validation":"An isolated check executed the exact Save, queue, loader, and field modules with controlled state and event doubles. Both requests succeeded. The transactions were A to B, then B to A. A control with an explicit B selection stayed in B.","appliedSummary":"Updated two files:

- `calendar-event-edit-save.mjs`: Unchanged calendar values now preserve the reloaded event’s calendar. Explicit moves remain supported.
- `test_calendarEventEditSave.js`: Added queued title and occurrence tests with Undo checks.

Commlint, syntax, whitespace, and six controlled checks passed. The diff follows the evidence record. No exact accepted Save example was found.

The new xpcshell tests remain unrun. The available build has unknown source stamps. Controlled checks do not prove Thunderbird runtime behavior.","changeSummary":"Use the reloaded event's calendar when draft.calendarId matches baseline.calendarId. Preserve explicit calendar changes.
